title: Rezk completion by the equivalence-groupoid resolution
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, Kan complexes, homotopy fibers and weak homotopy equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the Kan model structure from [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and Reedy fibrancy and functorial Reedy replacement from [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. A simplicial space is a functor $W:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$. In this statement a Segal space is Reedy fibrant and its consecutive-edge maps $W_n\to W_1\times_{W_0}\cdots\times_{W_0}W_1$ are weak homotopy equivalences for every $n\geq2$. Write $M_W(x,y)$ for the strict fiber of $(d_1,d_0):W_1\to W_0\times W_0$ at vertices $(x,y)$; Reedy fibrancy makes this a Kan complex representing the homotopy fiber. Its homotopy category $hW$ has the vertices of $W_0$ as objects, morphisms $\pi_0M_W(x,y)$, identities induced by $s_0$, and composition induced by the degree-two Segal map and $d_1$. Let $W_{\mathrm{eq}}\subseteq W_1$ be the union of components representing isomorphisms in $hW$. Call $W$ complete if $s_0:W_0\to W_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

Let $I[m]$ be the groupoid with objects $0,\ldots,m$ and exactly one morphism between each ordered pair of objects. Let $E(m)$ be its ordinary nerve, regarded as a simplicial space discrete in its inner simplicial direction. Let $F(n)$ be the outer representable simplicial space, with $F(n)_k=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([k],[n])$ discrete. For a simplicial set $K$, write $cK$ for the constant simplicial space on $K$. For simplicial spaces $A,W$, define their cartesian internal hom by
$$(W^A)_{n,q}=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sS}}(A\times F(n)\times c\Delta^q,W).$$
Its operators are precomposition in $F(n)$ and $\Delta^q$. The functors $I[m]\to I[m']$ induced by order-preserving maps make $E(\bullet)$ cosimplicial. Define a simplicial space $\widetilde W$ by
$$\widetilde W_{n,q}=(W^{E(q)})_{n,q};$$
its inner simplicial operators act simultaneously on the resolution index and the inner index. The collapse maps $E(m)\to F(0)$ induce a natural map $W\to\widetilde W$. Choose a functorial Reedy fibrant replacement $\widetilde W\to\widehat W$, a levelwise weak homotopy equivalence, and denote the composite by $i_W:W\to\widehat W$.

For every Segal space $W$, the simplicial space $\widehat W$ is a complete Segal space. The map $i_W$ induces a weak homotopy equivalence $M_W(x,y)\to M_{\widehat W}(i_Wx,i_Wy)$ for every pair of objects, and every object of $h\widehat W$ is isomorphic to some $i_Wx$. The construction $W\mapsto\widehat W$ and the maps $i_W$ are natural in maps of Segal spaces.

source.place: Rezk, A model for the homotopy theory of homotopy theory, Section 14, printed pp. 32-34: the displayed construction preceding Remark 14.1 and the proof of assertions (1) and (3), with Sections 4-6 for the definitions. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-homotopy result.

proof.text: The exponential formula gives $(V^A)^B\cong V^{A\times B}$ and $(U\times V)^A\cong U^A\times V^A$: both sides represent the same maps after currying. Put $A_m=W^{E(m)}$. For a monotone $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, precomposition gives $A_n\to A_m$; it commutes with precomposition in $F(k)$ and $\Delta^q$. Thus these maps and the inner operators commute and give the diagonal inner operators on $\widetilde W$. The unique collapse $I[m]\to I[0]$ gives the compatible maps $W=A_0\to A_m$. Functorial Reedy replacement supplies $r_W:\widetilde W\to\widehat W$ and makes $i_W=r_W\circ(W\to\widetilde W)$ natural. This proves that the specified construction and its maps are well-defined; it does not yet assert a Segal condition for $\widetilde W$.

source.place: Section 14, definition of the completion immediately before Remark 14.1; Section 2.3.

proof.text: Every $A_m$ is a Segal space by cartesian exponentiation. For any function $u:\{0,\ldots,m\}\to\{0,\ldots,n\}$, the induced $I[m]\to I[n]$ has an inverse up to natural isomorphism: choose the constant functor in the other direction at object $0$, and use the unique arrows for the two natural isomorphisms. Such a natural isomorphism is explicitly a functor $I[r]\times I[1]\to I[r]$, hence a map $E(r)\times E(1)\to E(r)$. Precomposition carries it to a categorical homotopy: its adjoint evaluates a map $b$ at $H(a,t)$. Therefore $A_n\to A_m$ has a common inverse up to categorical homotopies. The categorical-equivalence lemma gives weak equivalences on all mapping spaces and equivalences on homotopy categories for every simplicial operator, including degeneracies. This applies also to the collapses $W\to A_m$.

source.place: Section 14, proof of (1),(3), first paragraph; Sections 13.5 and 13.8.

proof.text: Fix an outer degree $k\geq1$. Let $B_m=(A_m)_0^{k+1}$ and $p_m:(A_m)_k\to B_m$ be evaluation at all $k+1$ vertices. Restriction along the monomorphism $\coprod_{i=0}^kF(0)\hookrightarrow F(k)$ is a Reedy fibration by the exponent lemma; its degree-zero map is $p_m$, so $p_m$ is a Kan fibration between Kan complexes. Write $R_m=(A_m)_1\times_{(A_m)_0}\cdots\times_{(A_m)_0}(A_m)_1$ with $k$ factors. Its vertex projection $R_m\to B_m$ is the pullback of the product of the $k$ Kan fibrations $(A_m)_1\to(A_m)_0^2$; a product horn lift is obtained coordinate by coordinate, so this projection is a Kan fibration. For $k=1$ the consecutive-edge map is the identity; for $k\geq2$ it is the Segal map. In either case the map $(A_m)_k\to R_m$ is a weak equivalence over $B_m$ between Kan fibrations. The forward direction of the arbitrary-base fiber criterion therefore makes its strict fiber map a weak equivalence. The fiber of $R_m$ at $(x_0,\ldots,x_k)$ is exactly $\prod_{i=1}^k M_{A_m}(x_{i-1},x_i)$. In every naturality square for $p$, the induced maps of these fibers are weak equivalences by step 2; finite products preserve weak equivalences, since realization preserves finite products and the components and homotopy groups of a finite product are the products of those of its factors. Consequently each naturality square is a homotopy pullback: since $p_m$ is a Kan fibration, the strict pullback $B_n\times_{B_m}(A_m)_k$ represents the homotopy pullback and the strict fibers of $p_n,p_m$ represent their homotopy fibers by the Kan model structure; the map to this comparison induces equivalences on every fiber, and fiberwise detection applies with the identity cover of its base. Apply the equifibered-diagonal lemma. Since diagonal commutes degreewise with finite products, its row-zero square identifies $W_k$ with the homotopy pullback of $\widetilde W_k\to\widetilde W_0^{k+1}$ along $W_0^{k+1}\to\widetilde W_0^{k+1}$. This identification uses the actual consecutive-edge maps.

source.place: Section 14, proof of (1),(3), first displayed square and its realization.

proof.text: Apply functorial Kan replacement to the cospans $\widetilde W_k\to\widetilde W_0^{k+1}\leftarrow W_0^{k+1}$ and $\widehat W_k\to\widehat W_0^{k+1}\leftarrow W_0^{k+1}$ before using the Kan-complex homotopy-pullback invariance lemma. Their three comparison maps are induced by $r_{W,k}$, $r_{W,0}^{k+1}$ and the identity; all are weak equivalences, using the product calculation in step 3. The lemma gives a weak equivalence of their homotopy pullbacks, compatible with the maps from $W_k$. Thus the step-3 comparison remains a weak equivalence with $\widehat W$ in place of $\widetilde W$. Right properness identifies the strict pullbacks of the Kan fibrations used below with their homotopy pullbacks. The map $W_0\to\widetilde W_0$ is bijective on vertices, because $(\widetilde W_0)_0=(W^{E(0)})_{0,0}=(W_0)_0$. It is therefore surjective on components, as is $W_0\to\widehat W_0$. For $k\geq2$, compare the consecutive-edge map from $\widehat W_k$ to the iterated homotopy pullback of $k$ copies of $\widehat W_1$ over $\widehat W_0$, over the base $\widehat W_0^{k+1}$. Over every tuple coming from $W_0^{k+1}$, step 3 identifies its fiber map with the Segal fiber map of $W$, which is a weak equivalence. Those tuples cover all base components, so fiberwise detection proves this Segal map is a weak equivalence. The degree-one matching object of $\widehat W$ is $\widehat W_0^2$, so Reedy fibrancy gives a Kan fibration $\widehat W_1\to\widehat W_0^2$. Each consecutive-edge strict pullback is therefore a pullback of Kan fibrations, and right properness identifies it with the iterated homotopy pullback just tested. Thus $\widehat W$ is Segal. The case $k=1$ of the same square gives precisely $M_W(x,y)\to M_{\widehat W}(i_Wx,i_Wy)$ as a weak equivalence.

source.place: Section 14, proof of (1),(3), passage from the realization squares to the Segal condition and mapping spaces.

proof.text: For any vertex $z$ of $\widehat W_0$, component surjectivity in step 4 gives $x\in W_0$ and a path from $i_Wx$ to $z$ in the Kan complex $\widehat W_0$. The map $(\widehat W)_{\mathrm{eq}}\to\widehat W_0^2$ is a Kan fibration: evaluation on all vertices is a Kan fibration by the exponent lemma, and restricting its domain to a union of components is again a Kan fibration (a horn filler remains in the component containing its specified vertex). Lift the base path $(i_Wx,\gamma)$ starting at $s_0(i_Wx)$. Its other endpoint is an equivalence arrow from $i_Wx$ to $z$. It gives the required isomorphism in $h\widehat W$. This proves essential surjectivity without assuming completeness.

source.place: Section 14, proof of (1),(3), surjectivity on isomorphism classes following component surjectivity.

proof.text: We need a property of the explicit diagonal construction before fibrant replacement. Extend $V\mapsto\widetilde V$ by the same formula to all simplicial spaces. It preserves cartesian products by the exponential formula. Put $E=E(1)$. Directly, $(\widetilde E_k)_q$ is the set of functors $[k]\times I[q]\to I[1]$, hence the set of functions $\{0,\ldots,q\}\to\{0,1\}^{k+1}$. (Maps out of $c\Delta^q$ into the inner-discrete target carry no extra information, since $\Delta^q$ is connected.) In particular there is a map $c\Delta^1\to\widetilde E$, natural in $k$, sending $\theta:[q]\to[1]$ to the function with value $(\theta(j),\ldots,\theta(j))$ at $j$. Its endpoints are the two constant-object sections. Hence a categorical homotopy $U\times E\to V$ becomes a simplicial homotopy $\widetilde U\times c\Delta^1\to\widetilde V$. The collapse $j:W\to W^E$ and evaluation $v:W^E\to W$ at object $0$ satisfy $vj=1$; the functor $H:I[1]\times I[1]\to I[1]$ with $H(a,0)=0$ and $H(a,1)=a$ on objects and the unique possible values on arrows gives a categorical homotopy $jv\sim1$ by sending $(b,t)$ to the map $a\mapsto b(H(a,t))$. Applying tilde therefore makes $\widetilde j$ and $\widetilde v$ homotopy inverses in every outer degree. Realization of the simplicial cylinder gives continuous homotopies, and homotopy invariance of all homotopy groups shows that $\widetilde j$ is a levelwise weak homotopy equivalence. No assertion that tilde is already Reedy fibrant is used.

source.place: Section 14, Lemmas 14.2-14.3; explicit calculation of the categorical-homotopy parameter.

proof.text: Let $Q_m=(A_m)_{\mathrm{eq}}\subseteq(A_m)_1$. All transition maps in step 2 are fully faithful on $hA_m$, so they preserve and reflect isomorphisms. Their maps on the invertible components of each mapping fiber are therefore weak equivalences too. The maps $Q_m\to(A_m)_0^2$ are Kan fibrations by the union-of-components argument in step 5. For $B_m=(A_m)_0^2$, the strict fiber of $Q_m\to B_m$ at $(x,y)$ is the union of invertible components of $M_{A_m}(x,y)$. For each $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, compare $Q_n$ with $B_n\times_{B_m}Q_m$ over $B_n$. Their fiber map at $(x,y)$ is exactly the invertible-component comparison just proved to be a weak equivalence. Fiberwise detection makes this a weak equivalence; since $Q_m\to B_m$ is a Kan fibration, this strict pullback represents the homotopy pullback. All naturality squares are therefore homotopy pullbacks, so the equifibered-diagonal lemma gives the homotopy-pullback square $Q_0\to\operatorname{diag}Q$ over $B_0\to\operatorname{diag}B$. There is an actual map $d:\operatorname{diag}Q\to(\widehat W)_{\mathrm{eq}}$: compose its inclusion into $\widetilde W_1$ with $r_{W,1}$. It lands in the indicated union of components, since every vertex of $\operatorname{diag}Q$ comes from $W_{\mathrm{eq}}$ and the Segal map $i_W$ preserves isomorphisms. Over the image of each $(x,y)\in W_0^2$, the row-zero comparison identifies the source homotopy fiber with the invertible components of $M_W(x,y)$. Step 4 identifies this with the invertible components of $M_{\widehat W}(i_Wx,i_Wy)$: full faithfulness of $hi_W$ reflects invertibility, since an inverse lifts by fullness and its two identities follow by faithfulness. The base cover $W_0^2\to\widehat W_0^2$ is surjective on components, so fiberwise detection gives that $d$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Section 14, final displayed square and identification of the realized equivalence-arrow space.

proof.text: Apply the equivalence-classifier lemma to each $A_m$. It gives compatible weak equivalences $(A_m^E)_0\to Q_m$. Their diagonals are a weak equivalence by bisimplicial diagonal invariance. By currying, the source diagonal is $\widetilde{(W^E)}_0$. Thus the composite $\widetilde{(W^E)}_0\to\operatorname{diag}Q\xrightarrow{d}(\widehat W)_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is a weak equivalence. Precompose with the weak equivalence $\widetilde j_0:\widetilde W_0\to\widetilde{(W^E)}_0$ from step 6. Its composite is exactly $s_0\circ r_{W,0}$: in resolution degree $m$, collapsing the extra factor $E$ and then restricting along its arrow $F(1)\to E$ selects the identity arrow in $A_m$. This equality survives both diagonal and the simplicial map $r_W$. Since $r_{W,0}$ is a weak equivalence, two-out-of-three gives that $s_0:\widehat W_0\to(\widehat W)_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is a weak equivalence. Together with steps 4-5 this proves all assertions. Every comparison just used is induced by restriction, currying, diagonal or the chosen functorial Reedy replacement, and these commute with postcomposition in $W$; the naturality asserted in step 1 consequently applies to the complete Segal spaces and their maps $i_W$.

source.place: Section 14, final paragraph proving completeness; Theorem 6.2 and Lemma 14.3.

Second reading adds the existing strict-fiber criterion, supplies the missing representable definition, and expands replacement, contraction and equivalence-arrow comparisons.

lean.statement: theorem rezk_explicit_completion (R : ReedyReplacement.{u}) (W : Space.{u}) (hW : IsSegal W) : IsComplete ((completion R).obj W) ∧ (∀ x y : (row W ⦋0⦌) _⦋0⦌, SSet.Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (mappingSpaceMap ((completionUnit R).app W) x y)) ∧ IsEssentiallySurjective ((completionUnit R).app W)
lean.note: The explicit equivalence-groupoid powers, diagonal, collapse map and composite completion map are actual functorial constructions. The theorem holds for every chosen functorial Reedy fibrant replacement, as in the source; no arbitrary completion or comparison map is substituted.
